title: Rabies Demands Quarantine; Dog-Trade Abolition Demands Accountability
excerpt: Rabies leaves no room for unsafe handling or hidden transport. Vietnam needs traceable quarantine, protection for families and pets, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Rabies gives families no second chance after symptoms begin. World Health Organization guidance states that rabies is virtually 100% fatal once clinical symptoms appear. Possible exposure requires immediate wound washing with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, followed by urgent medical assessment and post-exposure prophylaxis when indicated.

“Tradition” cannot replace traceability

Tradition does not answer basic safety questions: Where did each animal come from? Was it vaccinated? Was it examined? Was transport lawful? Were quarantine rules followed? A lawful food system needs records and inspection. Secret movement, uninspected slaughter, and evasion of checkpoints create enforcement gaps. They do not become safe because sellers call them customary.

“Farm-raised” needs proof

A claim about origin is not a record. It needs verifiable ownership, transport documents, veterinary oversight, and quarantine compliance. Without those controls, stolen companion animals and other untraceable animals can enter the same supply chain. Families lose pets. Communities lose confidence. Operators profit from secrecy.

Protect families. Close the gap.

Household rabies exposures and commercial-trade failures are separate problems, but both demand stronger biosecurity. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route; risk centers on infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes, and on handling sick animals or unsafe slaughter conditions.

Vietnamese communities can lead reform that protects children, families, workers, and companion animals. State rabies-control targets are not the same as SDE’s campaign demand: complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
